body:
After reading many reports and documents online about the recreational use of damiana and skullcap, coupled with the anti-depressant benefits of damiana, I decided to order some online and try it.
Firstly, I tried smoking 3 bowls of damiana and skullcap the day before I drank it as a tea, and it did nothing for me.  The smoke was very harsh and dry and burned the back of my throat every time I tried to take a hit.  The damiana tasted wonderful and smelled very pleasant, though. It also burned very quickly, so it got hot very fast.  Having failed to experience much from smoking the herbs (except a sore throat), I tried using them in tea the next day.
I brewed 1 tbsp (approx) of damiana and 2 tsp (approx) skullcap in boiling water for 6 minutes and added a teaspoon of honey to sweeten the tea, as it was a little bitter.  I drank the tea in a 15 minute time period.  It tasted very pleasant, and smelled even more wonderful than when it was burned.  It tasted very fresh and smelled almost like perfume.
Approximately 30 minutes later, I felt very relaxed and mildly euphoric.  I was very content doing what I was doing and the little things that used to bother me didn't anymore.  Soon after, I became fairly drowsy and wanted to take a nap, though I didn't.  The main effects of drowsiness wore off around 45 minutes later, but the euphoria (although mild) stayed for a couple hours.  I felt very social and I couldn't take the smile off my face.  Even more benefits presented themselves a little while later; I had been experiencing intestinal spasms (as a result of IBS) and menstrual cramps that day and after ingesting the tea they had completely disappeared!  I was amazed that the tea worked as well as the other medications I usually use to alleviate the symptoms.
All-in-all, I have enjoyed the experience.  If I were to compare the experience to any other drug I've tried, I would say it was like a very low-grade, subtle marijuana buzz, yet different in its own way.  I feel like I will be using damiana and skullcap in the future to alleviate symptoms of IBS and menstrual cramps, and even to relax after a long, stressful day.
